prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Produce a NEW UNLABELLED PNG background for a Chinese textbook diagram explaining heterogeneous graph input mapping and relational graph convolution. The two supplied external paper crops are mechanism references only: distinct typed entities/relations and relation-specific update paths. Do not copy their layout, text, colors or node identities. Independently design a clean, spacious wide composition, preferably about 2400 by 1350 pixels.

Scientific content is authoritative. Distinguish authors from papers using small flat author bust glyphs and simple flat paper-sheet glyphs. Exactly TWO author neighbours send a writing relation to ONE target paper; exactly TWO paper neighbours send a citation relation to the SAME target paper. Writing and citation use distinct line style AND color. All four directed edges point into the target; no author-to-author edge, no citation from an author, no false extra edge. Leave adjacent blank room for node/edge labels. This compact graph is an input example, not the computation graph itself.

Show the calculation with two parallel relation lanes, one for author inputs and one for paper inputs. In each lane, input features undergo one TYPE-specific input mapping into a common representation space, then a relation-specific matrix transform, then normalized within-relation aggregation. Small flat vectors or matrix grids may illustrate these operations. Keep these repeated objects flat, sparse, and clearly separated. Both aggregated relation outputs merge into one common cross-relation SUM/activation, then one updated target representation. A THIRD independent self-state path, from the target's previous representation through its own transform, also enters this same sum. Do not attach the self path to either relation aggregator. The arrows must express all three inputs to the final merge. No connections between the two relation lanes before that merge. Reserve open space on the merge and output for genuine formula labels to be added later.

Layout is your decision: make scientific objects richer than a chain of empty cards, but leave generous clear areas for short real-font headings and labels in every module. Do not fill the whole image with cards. Use white modules with colored outlines where possible; only meaningful relation lanes may have extremely pale independent grouping regions. Same authors use the same glyph, same papers use the same glyph. Those glyphs are mechanism objects, not extra decorative badges. No more than one decorative icon per module; preferably no decorative icons on math operations. Author/write semantic lane Lancet blue #7B95C6; paper/citation lane green #67A583; self-state peach #F59C7C; final merge/output restrained cyan #49C2D9. Fill only with uniform opaque 18% or 22% mixtures with white. Thin smooth neutral gray arrows except relation-encoding edges. Main neutral ink #3B4252. Consistent thin line weight, clear endpoints and arrowheads, no arrows through nodes or future label areas.

Absolutely NO text, title, letters, numbers, formulas, punctuation, pseudo-text or watermark anywhere. Vector/matrix cells are blank. All typography will be added afterwards using actual Source Han Sans Normal, LXGW WenKai and Fira Math fonts. Pure #FFFFFF background and entirely even pure fill colors. Flat front-facing 2D; no perspective sides, 3D blocks, spheres, extrusion, shadow, gloss, gradient, paper/canvas texture, grain, noise, ripples, stripes or clouded color variation. Keep margins airy and all objects completely inside the canvas.
